feedback: Review of the widened-span candidate, based only on earlier races. Iteration 1 (sensors at +/-0.04 m, ki 0.3, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.4) ended all 60 trials off_track with progress 0.04 to 0.13. Each run recorded one line-loss event, and max_error stayed pinned at about 0.061 m, just above the 0.06 m limit. Steering_oscillation was low (0.06 to 0.07), so the failure is steady drift, not jitter. Iteration 0 showed the same pattern at +/-0.02 m, so the failure point did not move when the span changed from +/-0.02 to +/-0.04 m. The candidate is valid: five sensors match five weights, all x-positions are within +/-0.08 m, and every controller field is inside its limit. Its geometry change is the one the earlier evidence points to, since a +/-0.06 m span keeps the line visible beyond the 0.06 m off-track limit. Two caveats. Scaling the outer weights to 1.5 raises the effective proportional gain at the outer sensors from 3.0 to 4.5, so oscillation may rise even though it was low in iteration 1. The rationale also changes weights along with span, so any gain effect is not separated from the geometry effect. The race is needed to see whether the wider span removes the line loss and the max_error pinning. Use the telemetry as follows. If line_loss_events is 0 but max_error still reaches 0.06, the robot cannot steer hard enough on bends: lower kp to about 2.5 (this also offsets the 1.5x weight scaling) before changing speed. If line_loss_events is 0, max_error stays under 0.06, and completion_time is above 3 s with progress near 1, raise base_speed to 1.7. If the drift is steady, oscillation stays low and max_error still grows over the run, raise ki from 0.3 to 0.5. Change one group of fields per revision.
requested_changes: Keep the +/-0.06 m span with weights +/-1.5 at the outer sensors and +/-0.75 inside, as iteration 1 showed the +/-0.04 m span still lost the line at about 0.061 m. Then judge the race on line_loss_events and max_error.

If the next race shows line_loss_events 0 but max_error still reaching about 0.06 (the robot cannot steer hard enough on bends), set controller.kp to 2.5 to offset the 1.5x weight scaling, keeping all other fields.
If the next race shows line_loss_events 0, max_error below 0.06, and completion_time above 3 s with progress near 1, set controller.base_speed to 1.7 and keep the other fields.
